title: A Review of Virtual Tutoring Systems and Student Performance Analysis Using GPT-3
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how virtual tutoring systems, particularly those involving GPT-3 and related AI approaches, may support student performance and feedback in education. The review is guided by three questions: the advantages and disadvantages of virtual tutoring compared with face-to-face instruction, the effectiveness of GPT-3 for improving tutoring experiences and learning outcomes, and future directions for AI-driven tutoring and student performance analysis.

The intervention studied is not a single implemented program but the body of literature on virtual tutoring, online tutoring, AI in educational technology, and GPT-3 integration in education. The authors conducted a systematic review using keyword-based searches across databases including IEEE, Science Direct, Springer, Wiley, Google Scholar, PubMed, and SCOPUS for publications from 2017 to 2024. They report that 130 studies were excluded and six articles were retained for data extraction, with PRISMA adapted to structure the review.

The population covered across the included literature is mixed, spanning both K-12 and higher education students, including vulnerable children as well as university learners. The context is primarily online and virtual learning environments rather than face-to-face classrooms. The review also discusses implications for educators, especially around feedback, adaptive learning, automated assessment, and the use of student data to personalize instruction.

The main conclusions are that GPT-3 and AI-enabled virtual tutoring show promise for personalizing learning, increasing engagement, providing immediate feedback, and potentially improving student outcomes. At the same time, the authors emphasize important limitations and implementation concerns, including bias, privacy, cultural relevance, accessibility, and the need for human oversight. They conclude that GPT-3 should be used as an assistive tool alongside educators and call for more longitudinal, ethical, and context-sensitive research on scalable deployment.

finding.finding_summary: The review concludes that GPT-3 has potential to personalise learning experiences, provide real-time assistance, and generate personalised feedback, with existing studies described as suggesting benefits for student performance. The paper does not provide pooled effect sizes or direct quantitative estimates.

The paper states that GPT-3-powered virtual tutors can create more dynamic and interactive educational experiences and may enhance student engagement. This claim is presented as a narrative synthesis without pooled quantitative evidence.

The review notes that GPT-3 can support automated grading and timely feedback, and that its language-processing capabilities enable prompt, individualised assistance in virtual learning environments. No quantitative efficiency metrics are reported.
